summary: This work proposes circular-modulated concatenated continuous driving (CMCCD) for silicon spin qubits, which simultaneously modulates both amplitude and phase of the microwave drive to generate a circularly polarized field that cancels counterrotating terms in the second rotating frame, eliminating systematic pulse-area errors from the imperfect rotating wave approximation. Experimental implementation on an isotopically purified $^{28}$Si-MOS quantum dot demonstrates that CMCCD achieves higher gate fidelity than conventional amplitude- or phase-modulated CCD schemes and exhibits significantly improved robustness to static detuning and Rabi frequency errors without requiring the second rotating wave approximation.
motivation: Conventional concatenated continuous driving schemes using either amplitude or phase modulation alone suffer from residual counterrotating terms in the second rotating frame that limit gate fidelity, particularly for fast gates where the rotating wave approximation breaks down.
method: The authors implemented CMCCD with equal amplitude and phase modulation ratios ($\alpha_A = \alpha_P = 1/2$) on an electron spin qubit in a silicon quantum dot, performing chevron measurements, Rabi oscillations under artificial detuning and Rabi errors, and randomized benchmarking at modulation strength $\epsilon_m = \Omega_0/4$ with $\Omega_0/2\pi = 2.2$–$3.6$ MHz.
result: CMCCD achieved state infidelity $\sim 10^{-3}$ at zero error and maintained robust gate fidelity over $\pm 20\%$ Rabi frequency variation, compared to bare qubit infidelity $\sim 10^{-2}$ at similar error levels; the device exhibited $T_2^{\mathrm{CCD-Rabi}} = 12.8$ µs and $T_2^{\mathrm{CCD-Ramsey}} = 17.7$ µs in the double-dressed state, demonstrating superior tolerance to both detuning and drive amplitude fluctuations versus conventional CCD schemes.
